script: GB -0.5 with a 54 total is a pick'em shootout, so Dallas will not be able to hide behind Javonte Williams' 50 carries and 205 yards from weeks 3-5, and Green Bay will not grind with a split of Marshawn Lloyd 21/55 and K.Johnson 19/74. Both passing games stay live because Dak Prescott (0.26 EPA with no blitz) and Jordan Love (0.25 EPA with no blitz) are the engines, and a one-score spread does not produce a fourth-quarter run script for either committee.
who_goes_off: Christian Watson is the go-to: 286 receiving yards on 21 targets and 293 air yards over weeks 3-5, a 95.3-yard pace, into a Dallas defense that has allowed 17 passes of 20+ on 143 attempts. CeeDee Lamb's 310 yards on 35 targets is the Dallas version, but Green Bay has allowed only 8 explosives on 172 attempts, so Watson has the cleaner explosive matchup.
weak_spot: Dallas' middle is the real hole at 11.56 YPA on 25 attempts, versus 7.66 left (50 att) and 7.73 right (63 att), which is the lane for Watson's 293 air yards and Tucker Kraft's 20 targets at 65 air yards. Green Bay has no such lane — 6.73 left, 6.54 middle, 6.03 right — and Dallas' other leak, 5.31 rush YPC with 20 runs of 10+, is wasted on a Green Bay committee that has not produced a 4-YPC back in Lloyd (2.6).
injury_fallout: No injury report is in the pre-kickoff data, so weeks 3-5 usage holds: Williams 50 carries versus Tyler Goodson 9, Lamb 35 targets and George Pickens 27 versus Ryan Flournoy 18 and Jake Ferguson 15, and Lloyd 21 carries sharing with K.Johnson's 19 while Watson (21 targets) and Matthew Golden (27) split the Green Bay downfield work. Nothing in the data promotes Goodson, Pierre Strong (5 carries, 7 yards), or Bo Melton (6 targets, 20 yards) into a featured role.
qb_vs_blitz: Dak is 0.06 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=69) against 0.26 with no blitz, and Green Bay blitzes 34%, so Lamb's 300 air yards and Pickens' 280 air yards are the Dallas shots most at risk, with Williams' 11 targets at -3 air yards the checkdown outlet. Love is -0.10 vs blitz (n=78) but 0.25 without, and Dallas blitzes only 27%, so he should live in the clean-pocket split that has produced Watson's 286 yards.

picks.why: Watson is at 95.3 receiving yards per game (286 on 21 targets, 293 air yards, so he is cashing the downfield targets) against a 76.5 line, and Dallas has allowed 17 gains of 20+ on 143 attempts plus 11.56 YPA in the middle. Love sees a blitz on only 27% of dropbacks, the split where his EPA is 0.25 rather than -0.10, so the 76.5 number sits about 19 yards under the recent pace.

Lloyd is at 18.3 rush plus 16.3 receiving per game (21 carries/55 yards, 10 targets/49 yards), 34.6 combined against a 58.5 rush+rec line. Even repricing his 7-carry share at Dallas' 5.31 YPC allowed is about 37 rush yards plus 16 receiving, still short of 58.5, and a 54 total with Love at 0.25 EPA unblitzed does not hand a back who is splitting with K.Johnson (19 carries, 74 yards) a 10-carry script.
